summary: Northbridge Defense Systems: request documentation for offline bundle signature verification + key rotation assurances
description:
Issue summary
Northbridge Defense Systems (air-gapped / regulated) is requesting:
1) Customer-facing documentation for verifying signed offline bundles during installation and as a pre-flight step (fully offline).
2) Written assurances/details around signing key custody and key rotation, including how older bundles remain verifiable and what happens on key compromise.

Impact
Blocking Security review / procurement gate for Private (on-prem, air-gapped) pilot. Customer needs a document they can attach to their internal ATO package.

Customer request (verbatim notes from SE call)
- “Show us the exact verification procedure we can run in an air-gapped environment, and what evidence it produces.”
- “What is your rotation cadence and how do you prevent a key rotation from breaking verification for previously delivered bundles?”
- “How do you revoke a compromised key and how will we learn about it offline?”

Environment
- Deployment type: Redwood Private, air-gapped/offline media transfer
- Installer: redwood-private-installer (customer evaluating pre-GA offline bundles)
- Networking: no outbound network allowed from install environment

What we provided so far
- Verbal overview of bundle-level signing + per-artifact digests, fail-closed verification, and break-glass override requiring explicit acknowledgement.
- Mentioned that keys are KMS/HSM-backed with least-privilege access and an incident procedure.

Requested deliverables
A) Verification guide (customer-facing):
- Where signature + manifest live in the bundle
- How to run verification (CLI), expected output, exit codes
- What logs are written and where
- Troubleshooting guidance for common failures (tampered media, partial copy, wrong bundle version)

B) Key management / rotation statement (customer-facing):
- Key custody (KMS/HSM), access controls, audit logging
- Rotation cadence and overlap strategy (old bundles remain verifiable)
- How verification discovers the right public key (key IDs)
- Compromise handling: revocation approach, customer notification, guidance on accepting/rejecting bundles signed by a compromised key
- Explicit statement: verification does not require any online calls

Internal routing / owners
- Solutions Engineering (primary): Markus Klein
- Security review + key management language: Marcus Lin / Olga Petrov
- Docs packaging: Kira Thompson / Elliot Price

Next steps
1) Provide customer with Redwood Private signed bundle verification doc (draft is acceptable) and key rotation FAQ.
2) Confirm whether customer requires artifacts in PDF format and/or a signed letter (Security may need to approve).
3) Track any delta between draft docs and GA behavior (avoid over-committing on exact command flags if still moving).

References
- Docs draft PR: redwood-docs/pr_1332
- Installer verification PRs: redwood-private-installer/pr_1042, pr_1051
- Confluence: runbook-verify-offline-bundle; break-glass-policy-offline-verification; threat-model-offline-artifact-signing; offline-bundle-signing-control-mapping
comments: 2026-02-10 09:14 Dev Patel (Support) — Created from SE handoff. Customer wants written verification steps + key rotation assurances for ATO. Assigning to Markus Klein (SE) with Sec as stakeholders. Priority P2 due to procurement gating, not prod incident.

2026-02-10 11:02 Markus Klein (SE) — I’ll own customer response. Requesting Security to provide approved language re: key custody/rotation/compromise. @Marcus Lin @Olga Petrov: can we provide a short customer-facing statement and point to control mapping page?

2026-02-11 08:37 Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — We can provide approved language at a high level (KMS/HSM-backed signing service, audited access, dual-approval for key ops). For rotation: plan is overlapping trust (new key introduced while old remains trusted for verification for a defined window) + key-id in signature metadata. For compromise: revocation list distributed with offline installer updates + out-of-band customer notification via support/CS. Please don’t promise a specific cadence beyond “at least annually and on compromise/events” until Key Mgmt runbook is finalized.

2026-02-11 13:18 Olga Petrov (GRC) — For ATO packages, customers typically want: (1) control mapping (SOC2/ISO-style) and (2) process summary. It’s OK to share the control mapping page + a 1–2 page memo. I can draft a customer-safe excerpt (no internal system names beyond KMS/HSM, no account IDs).

2026-02-12 10:06 Kira Thompson (Docs) — Draft customer guide is in redwood-docs/pr_1332; includes: verify step, troubleshooting, and FAQ. It references the CLI as `redwood-private-installer verify-bundle --bundle <path>` and documents exit codes. Note: exact flag name may change; we should caveat as “preview” if customer is on pre-GA installer.

2026-02-12 16:45 Markus Klein (SE) — Sent customer an email with: (a) verification guide draft (exported PDF), (b) key rotation/compromise statement drafted by Security (reviewed by Olga), and (c) link list to the relevant Confluence pages as supporting material. Asked if they need a formally signed letter or if the memo is sufficient.

Shared links (customer-safe):
- Offline bundles overview
- Verify offline bundle runbook (customer-facing section)
- Break-glass policy (acknowledgement language)
- Threat model (sanitized)
- Control mapping (SOC2/ISO mapping)

Awaiting customer confirmation.

2026-02-14 09:22 Dev Patel (Support) — Customer replied: they specifically asked “how do we verify older bundles after rotation?” Markus, please confirm answer: we include key-id in signature envelope and installer ships with a trust store that can include multiple public keys; rotation adds new key without removing old until end-of-support window (or until explicit revocation).

2026-02-14 10:03 Marcus Lin (Security Eng) — Confirmed. Add one more nuance: if an old key is revoked due to compromise, verification should fail for new installs unless customer explicitly accepts risk (break-glass) and logs acknowledgement. We should describe the decision path and that we will provide updated installer/trust store offline.

2026-02-17 15:28 Markus Klein (SE) — Responded to customer with clarified wording:
- Signatures include a key identifier.
- Installer’s offline trust store supports multiple keys concurrently.
- Rotation introduces new key while retaining old for verification of already-issued bundles for a defined deprecation period.
- If a key is compromised, we revoke it and distribute an updated trust store via offline channels; customer is notified out-of-band. Break-glass is available only with explicit acknowledgement and is auditable.

Customer indicated this meets their documentation requirement pending internal review.
2026-02-21 10:40 Dev Patel (Support) — No further questions from customer; marking Resolved. If customer requests a formally signed letter, reopen and route to Security/Legal.
resolution: Provided customer-facing draft documentation for offline bundle signature verification plus Security-approved key custody/rotation/compromise statement; shared supporting Confluence references and clarified how older bundles remain verifiable across rotations (multi-key trust store + key identifiers).
attachments: Exported PDF: Redwood Private — Verifying Signed Offline Bundles (draft, from redwood-docs/pr_1332)
Memo: Offline Bundle Signing Key Rotation & Compromise Handling (customer-safe, Security/GRC reviewed)
